subjects.displayTitle: Living in the world with a free heart
subjects.introduction: A heart entirely free, yet busy with rent, work and the needs of others: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likens the task to going through water without getting wet, and admits it is the subtlest of psychological questions. Bahá’u’lláh settles what is at stake by defining the world not as fields, rivers, trade or the ties of family, but as whatever turns a person aside from God, and He warns that an admirable deed or an inherited creed can serve as that veil just as well as gold. The inquiry then becomes personal: where does my attention rest, and what would I grieve to lose? Fattened cows and nesting birds, mirages and shifting sand, palaces emptied into tombs, all unsettle the usual measures of success and ask whether wealth or power ever made anyone free. Detachment of this kind is not withdrawal; it shows itself as kindness, honest labour and moderation inside ordinary responsibilities. From here the road leads on to the inner meaning of detachment, to the restless hunger of greed, and to the difference between a material and a spiritual civilization.
subjects.arc: Open with the difficulty of combining inward freedom and practical responsibility; clarify several meanings of worldliness; explore attention, desire and recognition; examine images of transience and the limits of wealth or power; read historical addresses within their settings; return through prayer to kindness, moderation and service.

order.why: Define the world by its power to obstruct recognition.
Open with the practical paradox of detachment while solving material problems.
Distinguish attachment from the created bounties themselves.
shortened: The similitude of the world is as a shadow - at times it existeth and at times it existeth not. No wise one would attach their heart to such a thing, but rather would consider it vain.
Think not that the world and what is meant by it are the ordained bounties therein or its varied ornaments, for these things are the creations of the Truth and the manifestations of His handiwork.

order.why: Give the objections to withdrawal and their reported answer room to be heard.
Keep social and economic relations within the account of human progress.
shortened: He brings to them divine qualities and frees them from indifference towards God, from prejudices which are founded on ignorance, from animal instincts, and from the attachment to the material world and the surrender of self to it - by attachment to the material world, I do not mean social intercourse and economic relations upon which the progress of the world depends, but I mean the ascendency of the lower life over the higher ideals of human society.

order.why: Question whether material poverty or wealth measures inward freedom.
Join detachment of heart to kindness in relationship.
Restate worldliness as what prevents turning toward God.
shortened: The world is that which preventeth men from turning toward God, not what heedless servants have understood it to be. Thus hath it been sent down from the Pen of our Most Glorious Lord in a preserved tablet.

order.why: Extend examination to customs, creeds and apparently excellent deeds.
Read the several meanings of worldly ornaments explicitly.
Consider the Báb’s account of inward orientation.
Let the comparison with animals challenge a merely material measure of life.
shortened: No matter how much man gains wealth, riches and opulence in this world, he will not become as independent as a cow. For these fattened cows roam freely over the vast tableland. All the prairies and meadows are theirs for grazing, and all the springs and rivers are theirs for drinking! No matter how much they graze, the fields will not be exhausted!

Thus it becomes evident that in the matters of this world, however much man may strive and work to the point of death, he will be unable to earn the abundance, the freedom and the independent life of a small bird. This proves and establishes the fact that man is not created for the life of this ephemeral world--nay, rather, is he created for the acquirement of infinite perfections, for the attainment to the sublimity of the world of humanity, to be drawn nigh unto the divine threshold, and to sit on the throne of everlasting sovereignty!

order.why: Read the birds as an image of contentment.
Compare outward sovereignty with the freedom of a bird.
shortened: Is the king free as the bird is free to fly upward? The king's head is often heavy with anxiety and the things of this world which hold him down.

order.why: Ask what makes human life distinctive beyond comfort.
shortened: If nobility and life were material, birds live much better than humans. How much effort humans must make and what difficulties they must accept for life! But the birds of mountain and desert without effort have their homes in the highest mountain peaks or tree branches, and all the plains are their vista, and all the harvest fields and seeds are their wealth. No human has such comfort. If physical comfort were the measure, certainly their life is greater than human life.

order.why: Continue the challenge to pleasure as the sole purpose of existence.
shortened: If the purpose of existence is sensual life and pleasures, then animal and man are equal. Happiness and pleasure are rather the possession of the bird and not those of distressed and sorrowful men.

order.why: Connect the economic question with heart and spirit.
Hear the summons to awaken amid a passing opportunity.
shortened: And again He saith: "O bond slave of the world! Many a dawn hath the breeze of My loving-kindness wafted over thee and found thee upon the bed of heedlessness fast asleep. Bewailing then thy plight it returned whence it came."

order.why: Turn awakening toward the direction of thought.
shortened: The commercial man awakes with the thought of commerce; the inventor awakes with the thought of his inventions; the banker with the thought of money. But you, when you awake, must at once think of God and begin the day with an earnest desire to attain to the will of God and His good pleasure.

order.why: Read wakefulness against the image of a sleeping world.
shortened: What delusions are these, what rebellion is this, what ignorance is this, and what disobedience is this - that they are heedless of God yet alert to the world, asleep to the Kingdom yet awake to the realm of dust!

order.why: Allow awakening to unsettle the presumed advantages of learning.
shortened: How many a learned one cast the Book of God behind his back, and how many a mystic was seized by the winds of the world and withheld from the Most Exalted Horizon, and how many a sleeper heard the Call, arose and turned to His luminous horizon.

order.why: Examine the gap between confessing transience and clinging to it.
Continue the tension between acknowledged impermanence and actual choice.
Ask what understanding of mortality changes in practice.
shortened: Likewise reflect upon the baseness of the people of the world - they are occupied with that which they themselves acknowledge to be perishable, and are debarred from the life everlasting.

order.why: Name the differing centers of attention within ordinary aspiration.
Compare the desires that direct different lives.
shortened: Some of the people of the earth desire conquest over others; some of them are longing for rest and ease; others desire a high position; some of them desire to become famous; thank God that our desire is for spirituality and for union with God.

order.why: Read varied ambitions through the image of bonds.
Consider how even loved ones and gardens may become distractions.
Retain the personal address about a leading desire.
shortened: O thou fresh sapling in the orchard of the love of God!

Every maiden in this universe of life has a leading desire. One longs for wealth, and another for worldly honors, and yet another strives for adornment and decoration, while another yearns for pleasure and comfort.

order.why: Read the reported enumeration of egoism and insincerity.
Turn the examination toward self and desire.
shortened: The heedless souls who remain in the wilderness of self and desire and have not been guided by the dayspring lights of guidance are accounted as non-existent before the Truth.

order.why: Consider desire as a rival object of devotion.
Read intoxication as an image of lost awareness.
shortened: Verily, the people are intoxicated with the wine of their own desires to such an extent that they know not what they utter. They speak as their desires command them and purchase with their souls and their wealth the wrath of God, yet today they comprehend not.

order.why: Link absorption in desire to loss of reunion.
shortened: How many souls today are occupied with their selfish desires, to such extent that they are wholly veiled from the Truth and deprived of the wine of reunion.

order.why: Notice the possibility of being consumed without perceiving it.
shortened: Most people have been consumed by the fire of greed and desire while they perceive it not. Blessed is the soul that hath cast off the garment of greed and departed from the world out of love for God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Examine what a person treats as an object of worship.
shortened: Observe among the people how they have taken as their object of worship that world whose evanescence all acknowledge and confess, and how they remain debarred and shut out from the true Object of worship and from the rays of the Spiritual Sun.

order.why: Consider the dust that obscures a mirror.
shortened: What is the dust which obscures the mirror? It is attachment to the world, avarice, envy, love of luxury and comfort, haughtiness and self-desire; this is the dust which prevents reflection of the rays of the Sun of Reality in the mirror.

order.why: Describes the soul between spiritual refinement and worldly concerns.
Explore the effect of desire on sight.
shortened: Some, because their eyes are afflicted with the ophthalmia of desire, have failed to recognize Him and have contented themselves with this perishable world, passing by the eternal Kingdom.

order.why: Consider the narrowed vision of an exclusively outward life.
Read the relation between attention to body and soul.
shortened: They are heedless of being inflicted with a myriad of spiritual catastrophes, but do not desire the least harm to come to this transient body or be exposed to any jeopardy. They say whatever may happen to our soul, let it happen; but nothing less than utmost comfort for our body!

order.why: Keep the question of priority within bodily life.
shortened: They possess naught but pure fancy and find no eternal life save utter extinction. They have become slaves to self and remained cut off from the King of Kings; they have become servants of the body and remained heedless and veiled from the Lord of Lords.

order.why: Read the possibility of seeing without being withheld by worldly affairs.
shortened: The diverse colors of the world have occupied its people and deprived them of the Supreme Horizon, yet he who possesseth sight is not withheld by worldly affairs from the Most Great Prospect.

order.why: Test the security of wealth through the image of moving sand.
shortened: O divine servant! The wealth of the world is like sand dunes that winds carry from place to place each day. Today you observe a dune formed of sand in one location; tomorrow you see this dune completely scattered and dispersed with no trace remaining - the wind has carried it away and formed another dune from this sand two leagues away in another spot. In short, wealth and riches are like moving sand dunes - they come and go. Therefore, they hold absolutely no importance in the eyes of the people of knowledge.

order.why: Consider the empty shell of enduring fame.
Read appearance through the image of a mirage.
shortened: O blessed be this glorious, mighty station!

They whose eyes have been opened behold this world and its ornaments as a mirage which the thirsty one thinketh to be water. They are indeed possessed of insight. Nothing can prevent them from the Most Great Vision. They shall soon find themselves in an exalted station.

order.why: Follow the exhausting pursuit of an unreachable drink.
Examine sovereignty through mirage, vapor and shadow.
shortened: O seeker of true glory and nobility in the divine world! Nobility in the material world is an illusory matter and a blameworthy notion, for the highest degree of worldly glory is sovereignty and dominion over the world, and majesty and kingship. Yet when you look at reality, it is a body without soul, and a form without spirit and conscience. It is a reflection without foundation and a shadow without end. It is a mirage, not wine; it is appearance, not water; it is vapor, not cloud.

order.why: Notice the reversals produced by mistaken estimation.
shortened: O thou who gazest toward the Most Glorious Horizon!

Today all who are on earth run after a mirage and pursue a fleeting shadow. They have taken a vanishing drop to be a surging ocean and counted a lowly speck as a brilliant luminary. They have imagined the base earth to be the loftiest heaven and considered a heap of soil to be paradise supreme. They have conceived a transient fireplace to be an eternal garden and known an extinguished candle as a radiant flame.

order.why: Compare hunger for appearance with real nourishment.
Ask what the image of toys suggests about maturity.
Contrast a small possession with an ocean of possibility.
shortened: They have set their hearts upon this world of dust and water, and are unaware of heavenly bestowals. They have defiled themselves with the affairs of this transient world and are heedless of the eternal realm and everlasting life. They are content with a drop and are deprived of the ocean's waves. They are attached to an atom and are heedless and far removed from the Sun of Truth.

order.why: Read the nightingale and owl as contrasting objects of attraction.
shortened: This transient world of dust befits mere owls of ignorance. This gloomy dust-heap is only worthy of the birds of this mortal plane. The mystic nightingale maketh its home in the divine rose-garden and noble birds dwell in spiritual realms on high.

order.why: Keep the parrot and sweet nourishment within their poetic address.
Follow eagle, whale and lion toward an environment fitted to their powers.
Distinguish a cage from a nest through the prisoner image.
Read the reported description of ordinary dependencies as prisons.
Hear release into joy in the remembrance of one who has departed.
shortened: Ere this she was a captive in the fetters of material attachments; now she is established upon the throne of joy. Ere this she was a prisoner in the bond of this ephemeral world; now, like unto the birds of holiness, she hath winged her flight unto the realm of freedom.

order.why: Read the passage from narrowness to a spacious realm.
shortened: O thou goodly leaf!

This world is indeed a narrow and dark arena, while that world is supremely luminous, vast and near. In the twinkling of an eye one can hasten from this physical realm to the divine world, and race from this confined space to that boundless realm. Therefore, as much as thou art able, think upon that world rather than this world, and be intoxicated with that cup rather than this turbid chalice.

order.why: Consider the invitation toward a higher horizon.
shortened: However, when you close your eyes to this dark world and cast your gaze upward to the supreme realm, you will see all lights enduring, will see all eternal and everlasting, will see the reality of mysteries. Therefore, blessed is the pure soul that has not attached itself to the defilement and comfort of this transient world, but rather has become attracted to the purity and freedom and nobility of the eternal world.

order.why: Explore spiritual rebirth in relation to bodily life.
Read differing aspirations toward nature and the sublime.
Consider the invitation to seek more than natural existence.
Locate human nobility in divine inspiration.
shortened: The days shall pass and nothing but regret shall remain for the people of the world. The nobility of the human world lies in divine inspirations, not in worldly adornments.

order.why: Retain the reported contrast between human capacity and playing with dust.
Read the reported contrasts of palaces, hovels, light and nourishment.
Place earthly conquest beside its mortal ending.
shortened: O king of the country of knowledge!

The world-conquering kings strive for years with utmost vigor and devotion crying out and making sacrifices to conquer this country of dust, and rule this dark heap and at the end repose underneath it. Their flags get inverted and their ensigns upturned. Their radiance turns to darkness and their grandeur to lowliness.

order.why: Read Alexander as the source presents the limits of military renown.
Follow the historical example toward a different conception of greatness.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the signs of God! Alexander of Greece sought kingship and sovereignty and world conquest in this mortal realm, and in the end it became manifest loss and great harm and severe regret. Therefore seek not what he sought, and walk not in his path of conduct. Rather, open the world of meanings and seek sovereignty in the Merciful Kingdom and know true human greatness and glory in the divine world.

order.why: Retain the source’s particular account of Nadir and conquest.
Ask how outward conquerors may remain captive to themselves.
Separate world conquest from triumph in the divine estimation.
shortened: If today one should conquer the whole world, he hath not been nor shall he be, in the sight of God, powerful and triumphant.

order.why: Hear the address to the King of Paris in its textual setting.
Read the rejection of a throne within an address from imprisonment.
Consider the permanence claimed by worldly glory.
Compare passing majesty with enduring connection.
shortened: But that sovereignty retained no glory and that majesty had no lasting grandeur. However, his connection to the Sacred Threshold is an eternal sovereignty that will endure forever and remain steadfast.

order.why: Place service at the threshold beside sovereignty.
shortened: Therefore, set your thoughts upon the eternal sovereignty of the everlasting world, whose glory is heavenly, whose power is from the All-Merciful, whose grandeur is divine, and whose duration is everlasting.
I swear by the Ancient Beauty that servitude at the Sacred Threshold is better than sovereignty and dominion and rulership over the East and West of this earthly world.

order.why: Reconsider treasure through knowledge, love and truth.
Compare renown sought for itself with a life free from that pursuit.
Keep the account of Jam and the world’s unfaithfulness within its address.
shortened: O Jamshid-i-Rashid! His Holiness Jam saw no fidelity in this twisted world, tasted no sweetness, and attained not his desires. In truth, he saw few pleasant days. At times he was a wanderer in mountain and desert, bewildered and distracted in the grip of trials. At other times he was in endless hardship and difficulty. And in the end, he disappeared beneath the earth.

Observe how unfaithful this world is! How then can man set his heart upon it and become attached to it, unless his consciousness becomes unconscious? Otherwise he would become detached and withdraw to the side.

order.why: Retain the particular political history without making it a general claim about every public life.
shortened: In this world thousands of politicians came and went and published many important publications on earth, and now you find neither mention nor trace of them.

In truth, that poor soul was deprived of high office and the title Nizam al-Dawlih and honor and prosperity in Iran, gained nothing in the political world and saw no fruit, did not attain the fame that was his utmost desire, and left this world disappointed and sorrowful while each of the republicans considered himself greater than him.

order.why: Place outward luxury beside the common ending of earthly life.
shortened: Regard not this, that in these days, to outward seeming, they live in luxury and honour. For I swear by Him Who hath made true honour the exclusive portion of His loved ones, that though they repose on jewelled couches, in the eyes of God they dwell upon the dust; and soon shall they all return, in the utmost poverty and abasement, to that place wherein is neither lamp nor couch, neither friend nor comforter.

order.why: Read the movement from palaces to tombs.
Consider accumulation and the passing of its inheritors.
Ask what wealth can satisfy and what it cannot accompany.
shortened: Reflect upon those who have occupied themselves with the world and have turned away from their Lord, the Most Glorious. Can they consume of their wealth more than what God hath ordained? Nay, by thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise! Or can they carry it with them after the angel of death hath come from thy Lord, the Mighty, the Praised One? Nay, by thy Lord! They shall abandon what they possess with grief and sorrow and shall return to their abode in the nethermost hell.

order.why: Explore the uncertain inheritance of wealth and glory.
shortened: Night and day they are consumed by the fire of greed and deprived of the light of detachment. With all their soul they strive after wealth and glory, heedless of to whom this wealth shall revert the following day and who shall inherit this glory.

order.why: Consider ownership passing beyond the person who rejoices in it.
Read the paradox of wealth increasing poverty through boundless greed.
shortened: For gold leadeth men astray and rendereth its possessor the poorest of servants through the greed that God causeth to overcome him, which hath no bound. Moreover, this wealth impoverisheth him from all that hath worth before God, for it occupieth him in the world to such an extent that the remembrance of the Beloved is not mentioned in his heart. Apart from this, it shall not endure on earth and shall perish in less than a moment - this hath been witnessed by the worlds.

order.why: Consider loss in both worlds through misplaced attachment.
shortened: Those men who, having amassed the vanities and ornaments of the earth, have turned away disdainfully from God -- these have lost both this world and the world to come.

order.why: Read the transience of both wealth and might.
shortened: Fear not the might of ignorant divines, and be not gladdened by worldly wealth. Soon shall God's irrevocable decree seize both and bring them to naught.

order.why: Examine a life spent accumulating comforts.
Compare wealth with virtues as a measure of life.
shortened: We do not want spiritual progress, we do not seek human virtues, and we say "We are wealthy, we need not this bounteous feast. We have a flowing treasure, we want not the trouble of heart and soul."

order.why: Keep both poverty and riches from becoming a measure of worth.
shortened: Pay no heed to the world and set not thy heart upon wealth. Neither lament poverty nor boast of riches, for all these things have come from nothingness and unto nothingness shall they return.

order.why: Read the personal reassurance that lack of earthly treasure is no defect.
shortened: Most of the friends of Truth, in ages past and present, possessed no earthly treasures, and this has never been and is not now a defect, but rather is a manifest glory.
Take heed that the affairs of the world grieve thee not.

order.why: Return from possessions to enduring spiritual purpose.
Read the rooted tree as an image of tranquillity amid changing conditions.
Receive the counsel to remain fresh and verdant.
Connect inward joy with remembrance.
shortened: Be not saddened by the transient affairs of this base world. Keep thy heart illumined and joyous through the remembrance of the King of Oneness.

order.why: Read the invitation to rejoice in love amid passing conditions.
shortened: Dost thou grieve over this world? It shall pass away, by the Lord of the worlds! Rejoice in My love, which nothing created in all existence can equal. Verily, thy Lord is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Consider remembrance beyond the value of treasures.
Turn attention from grief over the world toward remembrance.
shortened: Let not earthly affairs grieve thee. Rejoice in My remembrance of thee and My turning towards thee from this forbidden spot.

order.why: Hear the counsel not to be overcome by worldly sorrow.
shortened: Beware lest the affairs of the world sadden you or its ornaments prevent you from My Straight Path. Fear God and follow not what ye possess, but rather follow that which ye are commanded by One Who is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

order.why: Read sadness itself as something that may turn attention away.
shortened: Beware lest the affairs of the world sadden thee and turn thee away from the Lord of all mankind.

order.why: Read comfort in relation to purposeful progress.
shortened: There is a vast difference between the soul who has consecrated his life to the joys, pleasures and delights of this mundane world and the soul who seeks nought else save the good-pleasure of the Lord, who devotes his rest and comfort to the progress of the Cause.

order.why: Turn toward wisdom and utterance.
Retain the reported advice to speak and act so that attachment lessens.
shortened: "Thou must do always something and speak in such a manner that the people's attachment to this world may become less.

order.why: Place love and unity at the center of the intended result.
Hear the call to set a cold and lethargic world aflame.
shortened: Lethargy and coldness have encompassed the world - set aflame the heart of the world! Darkness and heedlessness have surrounded creation - spread rays and lights upon the horizons! This flame is the mention of God and these lights are the knowledge of Truth.

order.why: Move from diagnosing attachment to asking for purification.
Pray for a hearing attentive to a wider reality.
shortened: I am occupied with the mention of this sorrowful world; bestow upon me an ear that may hear the melody of the Concourse on High, hearken to the song of the nightingale of Thy sacred gardens, and perceive the notes of the thankful birds with an attentive ear.

order.why: Make examination personal through the prayer of one who has been distracted.
shortened: O my Lord! The world hath occupied me from turning toward Thy horizon and hath prevented me from directing myself to the Dayspring of Thy Cause and the Dawning-Place of Thy Revelation. Therefore have I fled from myself unto Thee and have placed my trust in Thee.

order.why: Ask to remain free of what obstructs nearness.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O God of Names and Creator of heaven, to make me of those whom the world hath not kept back from turning toward Thy most exalted horizon, and whom the ornaments of earth have not prevented from drawing nigh unto Thee, O Lord of all beings and Ruler of the throne above and the dust beneath.

order.why: Read the plea for strength and certitude amid confusion.
Bring the emphasis back to divine attributes and spiritual qualities.
shortened: All must adorn themselves with divine attributes and spiritual qualities, for the world and all that is therein are not worthy of attachment, as that which perisheth deserveth not to be loved.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: Know thou that the world is the love of Mine enemies and the turning away from My sanctified, luminous and beloved Beauty.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: They behold the Lord of Lords established upon the throne of might, yet from Him they turn aside. The world hath so deceived them that they see neither right nor left. Lo! They know not.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: O thou who hast clung steadfastly unto the most sure handle! The world is full of strife and struggle. Each mind has its secret desire and every soul its different aspirations. This one is lost in the prairies of pleasure and diversion; and that one dissipates his life in the wilderness of commerce; one seeks eagerly for human glory while another hunts for rank and honour; some rise and fall as they struggle through the waste land of power and political appointment and still others are tortured and harassed at every turn as they sit upon their thrones.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: Had all the peoples of the world hearkened to the Word of Unity as it deserveth to be hearkened to, all would have turned unto God, detached from all else. The deceptive conditions and allusions of the world have debarred the nations from the most great bounty.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: Blessed are they whom the affairs of the world have not prevented from the supreme horizon.
This mansion of clay hath no worth, and these earthly temples have no station.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: Attachment to the world hath debarred the servants from the Lord of Names. Ere long they shall arise in lamentation and weeping, but shall find for themselves neither helper nor protector except if they repent and return unto God, the Mighty, the Kind.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: Beware lest the veils of the world and its manifestations and colors prevent you. Arise to promote the Cause with complete dedication and great steadfastness, and summon humanity unto truth through wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: The world is transient - look not unto it, but rather unto Him Who created and manifested it.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: But alas, some hearts became attached to the earthly world and remained veiled and deprived of those favors and assistances.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: The world hath deluded most of the servants. Blessed is he who hath cast it behind him, turning with his heart to the direction of the Intended One.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: The whole world hath been brought from nothingness into being for the recognition of the Ancient King, yet the pomp and vanities of the world have occupied all and prevented them from turning to the Most Exalted Horizon.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: The world is bewildered, for it is observed that the servants, out of love for two fleeting days, have closed and continue to close their eyes to everlasting, eternal blessings.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: Beware lest the affairs of the world hold you back or the clamor of the nations veil you. Draw nigh unto God, then aid His mighty and impregnable Cause.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: Give thanks to thy Lord for having aided thee in His love, and that the world did not prevent thee from turning toward the face of God, the Mighty, the Generous, even as My sister was veiled thereby from the Beloved of creation, choosing for herself the ornaments of the world and turning away from the good-pleasure of God, the Object of worship of the knowing ones.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: O thou who gazest upon the Face! The ornaments of the world of creation have prevented the people of the realm below from turning to the highest horizon. They are occupied with these things and are heedless and veiled from the Truth.

order.why: Clarify how this passage defines or diagnoses the world that can obstruct recognition.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! Fear God and follow not those whom the world hath deluded with its vanities in such wise as to have debarred them from My straight Path.

order.why: Examine how desire, attachment, or heedlessness shapes recognition in this passage.
shortened: Beware lest the conditions of the world and its ornaments, its favors, its bounties and its colors hold you back from turning unto the Dawning-Place of God's revelation, the Lord of all men.

order.why: Examine how desire, attachment, or heedlessness shapes recognition in this passage.
shortened: O spiritual youth! Every youth in this earthly realm is preoccupied with thoughts of this world and immersed in animal passions. Their thoughts are of food and drink, their pursuits the desire for pearls and shells, even the basest clay fragments. But the end result is regret and remorse.

order.why: Examine how desire, attachment, or heedlessness shapes recognition in this passage.
Examine how desire, attachment, or heedlessness shapes recognition in this passage.
shortened: Days pass by and one's life span comes to an end and no condition remains the same but there is a difference between the soul who passes his days in selfish desires and lusts and one who consecrates the duration of his life in suffering in the path of the lord of revelation.

order.why: Examine how desire, attachment, or heedlessness shapes recognition in this passage.
shortened: To-day the people of the world in general are self-occupied. They are either engaged in warfare, or in commercial pursuits, political pursuits, industrial pursuits, or agricultural pursuits. The interests of all are of a personal nature. They are thinking of self-aggrandizement, no desire save the destruction of the world, no purpose save the thoughts which are directed to the acquisition of their worldly possessions.

order.why: Examine how desire, attachment, or heedlessness shapes recognition in this passage.
Examine how desire, attachment, or heedlessness shapes recognition in this passage.
shortened: If all the kingdom of the world were offered to any person of insight to spend but one night with such as she in bed, he would surely refuse, yet she remained deprived of the Most Glorious Branch due to the ornaments of the world and its trappings, becoming intimate with the most hideous form in existence.
Such is the nature of the world and its adherents.
This hath occurred solely that all might be convinced that love of the world maketh the eye blind and the ear deaf, such that man cannot distinguish between the highest heaven and the lowest depths.

shortened: Is there a greater and more harrowing regret in this world than to spend one's physical energies in the awful road of lust, sinful passions, inordinate desires and the frivolities of the age! Because when the last curtain falls on such a dissipated life he finds to his utter remorse his nerves racked, his resources drained, his fortune wrecked, his hopes vanished, his opportunities lost, his visions vanished, his energies wasted and the light of his spirit extinguished!

questions: How do the different meanings of the world in these passages change your understanding of detachment? What forms of attachment might be difficult to recognize in oneself?
What would it mean to remain inwardly free while working, caring for others, and addressing material problems? Which passages help you explore that tension?
How do the images of birds, mirrors, prisons, and fleeting shadows challenge familiar ideas of success and freedom? Where do their meanings differ?
Why might awareness that possessions and power are temporary fail to change our priorities? What could help knowledge become a way of living?
What affinities and differences emerge when you read Matthew’s teachings on treasure and trust beside Qur’an28:77 and this compilation?
How might moderation, generosity, or kindness give practical expression to detachment? Which connected subject would deepen that inquiry?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 6:19–34 · Treasure, attention, and trust
references.note: Jesus connects treasure with the heart, contrasts service to God and wealth, and turns to birds and lilies while teaching trust and the priority of the kingdom. Compare these images with the compilation’s accounts of contentment and inward freedom. How does spiritual priority affect the way a person attends to daily needs?

What relationships between possessions, purpose, and responsibility become visible?
